Hi Kimberly,

Hope you're well — I'm Elaine (partnerships lead at Nebula Consulting), working with DataStack Labs on a joint Solution Accelerator we'd like to publish on AWS/GCP marketplaces and explore Redwood co-sell alignment. Before we start the intake, two quick questions so our PM and procurement folks can scope the ask: 

1) Credentialing & evidence: what minimum technical evidence do you need for a partner-built accelerator? (SaaS architecture diagram, runbook for private offers, SOC2 pointer?)
2) Metering & SKU mapping: can Redwood support per-instance hourly SKUs vs per-user tiers, and is there a template you prefer for mapping consumption to marketplace SKU names?

Attaching a short spec doc for the accelerator (prototype staging). We're targeting a soft launch in Q4 and would like to understand typical lead times for listing + co-sell enablement.

Attachments: solution-accelerator-specs.pdf (10 pages)

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

Thanks Elaine — welcome, and thanks for the spec. Quick summary + proposed next steps below.

Summary answers (high level):
- Credentialing: minimum items we need to start an intake: SaaS architecture diagram, data flow (incl. PII boundaries), deployment model (hosted vs private offer), and pointer to SOC2 or equivalent (if customer-facing). For accelerators that include a partner-managed connector to customer environments we also require an operational runbook and support SLA.
- Metering & SKUs: we support both hourly per-instance SKUs and usage-based metering. For marketplace listing we recommend mapping to 2–3 canonical SKUs (e.g., hourly-dev, hourly-prod, metered-GB) and using our metering-template (attached) to translate your internal metrics to marketplace metering events.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please confirm which deployment variants you plan to list (managed SaaS on Redwood-hosted infra, and/or private offer).
2) Fill the metering-template.xlsx (attached) with the mapping from your telemetry events to marketplace metrics. Ben/Olga can assist on the schema.
3) Share architectural diagram and the runbook (if private/offers included).
4) We'll open a co-sell intake internally and target a 4–6 week listing window after evidence is complete (shorter if no private-offer path).

Ben, Olga, Vivek — can you review the spec and the attached metering template? Ben: can you advise on any GCP/AWS-specific constraints we should call out? Olga: can you confirm our expected evidence checklist for partner accelerators (especially the private-offer runbook)? Vivek: heads-up from a commercial routing perspective — we may want to seed this as a co-sell candidate once the listing is in staging.

Happy to set a 30-min intake call if that helps — Elaine, any availability next week?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace Partnerships — Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Kimberly / Olga — skimmed the spec. A couple of practical items we should flag to the partner now so they can avoid rework: 

- Metering nuance: GCP requires distinct metric names for each SKU; avoid dynamic metric names that change per-tenant. Recommend they expose a stable event (e.g., ds.accelerator.session_seconds) and use dimensions for env. I'll add examples in the template.
- Private offer networking: if they want Private Offer with VPC-SC or customer-managed private endpoints, we need a network diagram + tested connectivity instructions. That often adds 2 weeks to validation.
- Billing reconciliation: ask them who will own invoice/be the billing party (DataStack or Nebula). If DataStack wants reseller flow we need reseller agreement in advance.

I attached an updated metering-template.xlsx with example rows (hourly-dev, hourly-prod, gb-processed). Olga — can you confirm the evidence checklist here and whether we need a pen-test report for accelerator connectors? If so, we should request an external pen-test timeline from Elaine.

Ben
